sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- the October tally] 37 ships were attacked in October, the highest monthly total since the start of the war, according to data from the Washington Institute for Near East Policy (via Reuters). [VERIFIED FACT -- the IMO total] The International Maritime Organization has confirmed 130 incidents, most of them attacks, in the region since the conflict began in late February, with at least 25 seafarers killed. [VERIFIED FACT -- the November tempo] There is 'little sign of attacks abating in November': three tankers hit Sunday Nov 8 (Navig8 Messi, Singapore-flagged, verified by Reuters video + Copernicus Sentinel-2 smoke plume; managed by Navig8, majority owned by ADNOC Logistics & Services) and two more caught fire Tuesday Nov 10 after hitting mines on the 'unauthorised route' (IRGC Navy via IRIB; recorded 2100-09/2300-01). UKMTO recorded 88 projectile strikes since hostilities resumed in early July (via EL7/Gulf News summary of UKMTO) and a tanker struck NE of Oman's Lima on Tuesday (UKMTO, recorded 2100-09). [VERIFIED FACT -- environmental damage] Attacks have caused oil leaking from damaged tankers; Reuters-verified video showed oil reaching the shores of Oman, and satellite imagery showed oil spills off Oman and the UAE; the Omani government did not respond to Reuters' request for comment Tuesday. [VERIFIED FACT -- Aramco office] Reuters-verified video showed damage to an Aramco office building in Riyadh following Ansar Allah-claimed missile strikes on Nov 8; the Saudi Energy Ministry said the building was targeted in an attempted attack, with debris causing limited damage, no injuries or fatalities. [CONTEXT -- the market vs the sea] On Tuesday crude prices hit two-month lows after US officials downplayed the need for additional military action against Iran, with analysts noting Trump's more conciliatory tone since the Republicans' Nov 3 midterm defeat. [CONTEXT -- the other side of the blockade] US forces continue enforcing the naval blockade of Iranian ports; a US military aircraft fired on and disabled the St Kitts-flagged cargo vessel M/V Huda on Saturday Nov 7 (CENTCOM; recorded via Nov 8 carriers, re-mentioned here as context, not new).
sections.what_verified: 3 distinct tiered publisher families: Reuters (T1, the piece itself) + IMO (T1, primary source for 130 incidents / 25 seafarers killed) + UKMTO (T1, primary source for 88 projectile strikes since July and the Lima strike). Jerusalem Post (T3) carries the identical Reuters copy and does NOT add a family (syndicated copy). Washington Institute has NO declared tier -- its October tally is reported with attribution only. EL7.AI / Gulf News summaries of the UKMTO weekly tally are unregistered carriers and do not count.
sections.what_disputed: COUNTING NOTE (not a contradiction, but narration must not merge the two): AP reported Oct 22, citing Lloyd's List, that 28 attacks on ships had been recorded in October -- that count was through Oct 22, while the Washington Institute's 37 is the full-month October total; different windows and different counting methods (Lloyd's List vs Washington Institute). Do NOT present 37 and 28 as competing totals for the same period. COUNTER-SCOPE: INTERTANKO's Oct 23 advisory says transits through the southern US-facilitated route are averaging over 30 per day with tankers ~90% of transits -- the corridor is not empty; PortWatch's near-zero AIS count (stale, Nov 1 observation) and the UKMTO weekly crossing tally (325, see notes) measure different things and must not be merged. No claimant has disputed the IMO's 130-incident confirmation. The Aramco office damage is 'limited, no injuries' per the Saudi Energy Ministry -- do not narrate it as a major strike on Aramco. The two Tuesday tankers' names/flags remain undisclosed by the IRGC.
sections.why_matters: October was the WORST month of the shipping war -- 37 ships attacked, the most since February -- and November is already burning: tankers on fire, oil washing onto Oman's shores, 25 seafarers dead. Washington says the war is 'effectively over'. The numbers say the war at sea is escalating.
sections.context: Background: HORMUZ BY THE NUMBERS -- Reuters Nov 10 data-wrap: 37 ships attacked in October (highest monthly total of the war); IMO confirms 130 incidents and at least 25 seafarers killed since Feb 28; oil spills reaching Omani shores; Aramco office damage verified

totw_analysis: Our read: October was the WORST month of the shipping war -- 37 ships attacked, the most since February -- and November is already burning: tankers on fire, oil washing onto Oman's shores, 25 seafarers dead. Washington says the war is 'effectively over'. The numbers say the war at sea is escalating. The fault line our audience is arguing over: October was the worst month of the shipping war -- 37 ships attacked -- and tankers are still burning in November while Washington talks peace. Who is winning the war at sea: the side that controls the strait with mines and missiles, or the side that says the blockade has already cost Iran $25bn in oil? Comment threads split between 'Trump started this war, not Iran' / praise for IRGC control of the strait and fear of escalation + grief for the 25 dead seafarers.
